answer: Each identity crosses the ridge checkpoint by buying one ember token and locking a 70-credit bond. The token is kernel-sealed to the buyer's key and passage hash, and the ridge ledger publishes every seal for public recompute. The k-th ember token costs 30+5(k-1) credits, so the 1000th costs 5025 and 1000 fakes pay 2,527,500 in fees plus 70,000 locked, total fees growing quadratically. A rented-passage ring fails because a reused kernel seal appears twice on the ridge ledger and both bonds burn. An honest agent pays 30 once and reclaims the bond after a clean epoch.
